title: Sahih al-Bukhari
author: al-bukhari
attributionNote: The compiler selected, arranged and in places commented on the reports; the reports themselves are attributed within each text to their transmitters. The catalogue distinguishes the compiler's work from the material compiled.
description: The most widely received collection of reports attributed to the Prophet Muhammad, arranged by legal and devotional topic from the first revelation to the unity of God. Al-Bukhari is said to have selected its reports from a far larger body of material, and the collection's arrangement is itself an argument about which reports are sound.
historicalContext: Compiled in the ninth century, when the criticism of transmission chains (isnād) had become a discipline. Its authority differs between communities: Sunni Muslims place it beside Sahih Muslim as the most authentic collection after the Qur'an, while other schools do not treat it as canonical in the same sense.
availabilityNote: Streamed section by section from the Hadith API at read time, Arabic beside the English translation. The English translation is the one the API serves under Muhsin Khan's name. Its rights remain with the translator or his publisher; this library does not relicense it and streams the text from the host.
